title: Heavy-Tailed Memory Traces in Long-Horizon Language Agents
description:
arXiv:2610.00010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon language agents increasingly rely on external memory as a frozen world model, yet current memory systems are usually judged only by task success or token cost. We argue that the missing object is the shape of memory use: under finite context and repeated retrieval, agent memory can concentrate on a small core while leaving rare states in a long tail where prediction errors accumulate.
